import pandas as pd

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv(DATA_PATH)

# Display the first few rows and basic information about the dataset
df_info = df.info()
df_head = df.head()

df_info, df_head

from scipy.stats import zscore

# Calculate z-scores for the transaction amounts
df['z_score'] = zscore(df['trans_amount'])

# Identify anomalies
anomalies = df[(df['z_score'] > 3) | (df['z_score'] < -3)]

# Count the number of anomalies
num_anomalies = anomalies.shape[0]

num_anomalies

from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from sklearn.metrics import precision_score, recall_score

# Prepare features and target variable
X = df[['trans_amount']]  # Using only transaction amount for simplicity
y = df['fraud_flag']

# Split the data into training and testing sets
X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(X, y, test_size=0.3, random_state=42)

# Train the logistic regression model
model = LogisticRegression()
model.fit(X_train, y_train)

# Make predictions on the test set
y_pred = model.predict(X_test)

# Calculate precision and recall
precision = precision_score(y_test, y_pred)
recall = recall_score(y_test, y_pred)

precision, recall

# Check the distribution of the fraud_flag
fraud_distribution = df['fraud_flag'].value_counts()

fraud_distribution

from imblearn.over_sampling import SMOTE

# Apply SMOTE to balance the dataset
smote = SMOTE(random_state=42)
X_resampled, y_resampled = smote.fit_resample(X, y)

# Split the resampled data into training and testing sets
X_train_resampled, X_test_resampled, y_train_resampled, y_test_resampled = train_test_split(
    X_resampled, y_resampled, test_size=0.3, random_state=42
)

# Train the logistic regression model on the resampled data
model_resampled = LogisticRegression()
model_resampled.fit(X_train_resampled, y_train_resampled)

# Make predictions on the test set
y_pred_resampled = model_resampled.predict(X_test_resampled)

# Calculate precision and recall
precision_resampled = precision_score(y_test_resampled, y_pred_resampled)
recall_resampled = recall_score(y_test_resampled, y_pred_resampled)

precision_resampled, recall_resampled

# Separate the fraudulent and non-fraudulent transactions
df_fraud = df[df['fraud_flag'] == 1]
df_non_fraud = df[df['fraud_flag'] == 0]

# Randomly sample non-fraudulent transactions to match the number of fraudulent transactions
df_non_fraud_sampled = df_non_fraud.sample(n=len(df_fraud), random_state=42)

# Combine the sampled non-fraudulent transactions with the fraudulent transactions
df_balanced = pd.concat([df_fraud, df_non_fraud_sampled])

# Prepare features and target variable from the balanced dataset
X_balanced = df_balanced[['trans_amount']]
y_balanced = df_balanced['fraud_flag']

# Split the balanced data into training and testing sets
X_train_balanced, X_test_balanced, y_train_balanced, y_test_balanced = train_test_split(
    X_balanced, y_balanced, test_size=0.3, random_state=42
)

# Train the logistic regression model on the balanced data
model_balanced = LogisticRegression()
model_balanced.fit(X_train_balanced, y_train_balanced)

# Make predictions on the test set
y_pred_balanced = model_balanced.predict(X_test_balanced)

# Calculate precision and recall
precision_balanced = precision_score(y_test_balanced, y_pred_balanced)
recall_balanced = recall_score(y_test_balanced, y_pred_balanced)

precision_balanced, recall_balanced
